routes.name: Visa-free short stay (Schengen)
routes.summary: Citizens of many countries can visit Germany without a visa for up to 90 days in any 180 days. You can't work. The Federal Foreign Office has the full country table.

other: Check the official table for your passport. Some waivers only cover biometric passports.
Entry/Exit System (EES) has been running since 12 October 2025: your face and fingerprints are checked and passports are no longer stamped.

stay.note: Can't take up paid work. You can apply for a residence permit after arrival in some cases.

sources.label: Federal Foreign Office: who needs a visa
Germany.info: EES

routes.name: Schengen Visa (short stay, type C)
routes.summary: If your passport isn't on the visa-free list, you need a short-stay visa for tourism, family visits or business trips. Up to 90 days in any 180 days.

other: Applies to nationalities that need a visa. Check the Federal Foreign Office table.

steps: Book an appointment at the German mission or visa center
Submit the full set of documents in person

fees.label: Short-stay visa (as listed by the German embassy in Accra)

routes.processing: The embassy page says about 14 days, can take longer. Apply at least 15 days before travel and up to 6 months before.

sources.label: German Embassy Accra: short-stay Schengen visa
Federal Foreign Office: who needs a visa

routes.name: Airport Transit Visa (type A)
routes.summary: Most travelers can change planes in the international transit area without a visa. Citizens of some countries need an airport transit visa even if they never leave the airport.

other: Required for nationals of: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cuba, DR Congo, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Ghana, Iran, Iraq, Jordan, Lebanon, Mali, Nigeria, Pakistan, Somalia, South Sudan, Sri Lanka, Sudan, Syria, Turkey (some exceptions).
Exempt if you hold certain valid visas or residence permits, for example from a Schengen state, Canada, Japan or the US, and stay in the transit area.
If you must enter Schengen during the stopover, you may need a regular visa instead.

routes.processing: One German embassy page says 15 calendar days. You can apply up to 6 months ahead.

sources.label: Federal Foreign Office: airport transit FAQ
German Embassy London: airport transit visas

routes.name: EU Blue Card
routes.summary: Residence permit for people with a university degree (or equivalent) and a qualified job paying above a set salary. Lower salary applies for shortage jobs, recent graduates and some IT specialists.

income.note: Gross. Lower threshold of 45,934.20 EUR for shortage occupations, recent graduates and IT specialists without a degree (needs Federal Employment Agency approval).

other: Job offer of at least 6 months matching your qualification.
Licence to practice if the profession is regulated.
IT specialists without a degree need at least 3 of the last 7 years in IT at university level.

stay.note: Contract length plus 6 months, up to 4 years.

sources.label: Make it in Germany: EU Blue Card
Make it in Germany: settlement permit

routes.name: Residence Permit for Qualified Professionals (Skilled Worker)
routes.summary: For people with a recognized university degree or vocational qualification and a qualified job offer. Federal Employment Agency usually approves the job.

other: Regulated professions need a licence to practice.
If you are over 45 and new to Germany, the job must pay at least 55,770 EUR gross per year (2026) or you must show adequate pension provision.
Non-academic vocational recognition generally takes 3 to 4 months.

stay.note: Contract length plus 6 months, up to 4 years.

sources.label: Make it in Germany: work as a qualified professional
Make it in Germany: settlement permit

routes.name: Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte)
routes.summary: A job search permit for skilled people. Qualify with a recognized qualification, or with at least 6 points in the points system. You can work part time while you search.

savings.note: Blocked account at this monthly amount for 2026, or a declaration of commitment.

eligibility.language: Points route: German A1 or English B2. No language needed with a recognized qualification.
other: Points: partial recognition 4, shortage occupation 1, work experience 2 to 3, German A2 1 / B1 2 / B2+ 3, English C1+ 1, age up to 35 2 / 35 to 40 1, prior stay in Germany 1, spouse meeting requirements 1.
Points route needs 6 points.
Work rights during the search: part-time job up to 20 hours a week plus job trials up to 2 weeks per employer. Page didn't list fees or says what happens above age 40. Confirm on the official page.

stay.note: Up to 1 year. Up to 2 more years possible if you have a job offer but can't yet get a work permit.

sources.label: Make it in Germany: Opportunity Card
Make it in Germany: Opportunity Card overview

routes.name: Residence Permit for Self-Employment and Freelancing
routes.summary: For starting a business (Section 21(1)) or working as a freelancer in a liberal profession (Section 21(5)). Business founders need proof of economic interest or regional demand.

other: Business founders: economic interest or regional demand, expected economic benefit, financing by own capital or a loan commitment, convincing business plan.
Freelancers: proof of funds for projects, any needed licences, enough money for living costs.
Over 45: proof of adequate old-age pension provision.

Settlement: business founders 3 years, liberal professions 5 years per the self-employment page. The settlement page lists 3 years for self-employed. Confirm with the foreigners authority. Fees weren't listed.

sources.label: Make it in Germany: self-employment
Make it in Germany: settlement permit

routes.name: Job Seeker Permit for Graduates of German Universities
routes.summary: After finishing a degree in Germany you can stay up to 18 months to look for qualified work. You can work in any job while searching.

eligibility.education: Degree from a German higher education institution
other: The separate job seeker visa for skilled workers abroad was not confirmed on a page I could read. For job searching from abroad, see the Opportunity Card.

sources.label: Make it in Germany: studying

routes.name: Residence Permit for Study (and visa to seek a university place)
routes.summary: For degree studies at a state-recognized German university. A separate visa lets you come for up to 9 months to look for a place.

savings.note: Blocked account minimum for 2026, or scholarship or declaration of commitment. Seeking-a-place visa: 1,091 EUR per month.

eligibility.language: Often German B2 if the program requires it
other: Admission to a state-recognized higher education institution.
Work while studying: up to 140 full days or 280 half days per year, or 20 hours a week. Page didn't give visa fees.

stay.note: Usually 2 years first, renewable for 2 more. Place-seeking visa up to 9 months, not renewable for that purpose.

steps: Get admitted or apply for the place-seeking visa
documents: Proof of financing (blocked account, scholarship or commitment)

sources.label: Make it in Germany: studying

routes.name: Visa for Vocational Training (Ausbildung)
routes.summary: For a company-based or school-based vocational training place in Germany. There is also a visa to look for a training place for up to 9 months.

other: Need a specific training place.
School-based training: at least 959 EUR net per month (2026) shown by blocked account, commitment or scholarship.
Company-based: training pay counts. Secure at 1,048 EUR gross or 822 EUR net per month (2026). Cover any gap with a blocked account.
Training-place search visa: under age 35, school certificate that gives university access, German B1, blocked account of 1,091 EUR per month, up to 9 months.

stay.note: Covers the length of training. After qualified training you can stay up to 18 months to find work.

sources.label: Make it in Germany: vocational training visa

routes.name: Family Reunion Visa (spouse and children)
routes.summary: Spouses and minor children can join a family member who lives in Germany. Spouses usually need basic German (A1) unless an exemption applies. Joining a German or EU citizen needs no income or housing proof.

eligibility.language: German A1 for spouses, with exemptions
other: Marriage must be valid under German law. Unmarried partners aren't covered by this route.
Joining a non-EU resident: the sponsor shows income and housing. No fixed amount on the page I read.
Spouse A1 exemptions: parent of a minor child, stay under one year, or easy integration expected (job offer, recognized degree).
Children must be under 18 and unmarried. Children over 16 have special rules. Single parent needs consent of the other custodial parent.
Same-sex marriages can qualify if valid under German law.
Rules for parents of adults and for refugees or subsidiary protection holders weren't checked. Fees weren't listed.

routes.processing: One embassy page says about 12 weeks after documents are complete.

sources.label: German Embassy Dar es Salaam: spouse reunification
Make it in Germany: children joining

routes.name: Working Holiday Visa
routes.summary: Up to 12 months in Germany with holiday jobs allowed. For citizens of 11 partner countries or territories.

other: Age limit 30, or 34 for South Korea.
Hong Kong applicants must be Hong Kong SAR residents.
Where to apply varies by country, for example Korea only in Seoul and Brazil only in Brazil.
Fees and documents weren't on the page. Check the local German mission.

sources.label: Federal Foreign Office: Working Holiday FAQ

routes.name: EU Free Movement
routes.summary: EU citizens need no visa or residence permit. You can stay 3 months with an ID. Longer stays need a recognized purpose like work, study, or enough money and health insurance. Permanent residence after 5 years.

other: Beyond 3 months: employment, self-employment, vocational training, job seeking, or enough means and health insurance.
You still register with your local residents registration office.
Permanent residence after 5 years of lawful, continuous stay. Shorter in some cases, such as retirement at 65 after 3 years.
EEA and Swiss rules are not covered here.

sources.label: Freedom of Movement Act/EU (English translation)
Federal Foreign Office: EU citizens FAQ

routes.name: Settlement Permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis)
routes.summary: Permanent residence. Time needed depends on your permit. Skilled workers usually need 3 years. Blue Card holders 27 months, or 21 with German B1.

eligibility.language: German B1 for most routes (Blue Card: A1 for the 27 month route)
other: Skilled workers: 3 years on that permit, B1, 36 months of pension contributions, living costs covered, Living in Germany test, enough living space.
EU Blue Card: 27 months, or 21 months with B1.
German graduates: 2 years on a skilled worker permit, B1, 24 months pension contributions.
Self-employed: 3 years, business must show sustainable development.
Spouses of skilled workers: 3 years, B1, and working at least 20 hours a week.
Fee up to about 150 EUR.

sources.label: Make it in Germany: settlement permit

routes.name: Naturalization (German citizenship by residence)
routes.summary: Apply after 5 years of legal residence. Since 27 June 2024 you can usually keep your old citizenship. The 3-year fast track from the 2024 reform was dropped in 2025.

other: Naturalization test, 33 questions, pass with 17 correct (BAMF). Test fee 25 EUR.
Permanent right of residence or an eligible permit such as an EU Blue Card.
Support yourself without citizen's allowance, with some exceptions.
Clean criminal record, and commitment to the democratic order.
Spouse and minor children can be naturalized together without meeting the 5-year rule themselves.

citizenship.note: 2024 reform cut the standard period from 8 to 5 years and allowed 3 years for very well integrated applicants. The federal cabinet approved ending the 3-year route on 28 May 2025, and the federal government lists it as dropped under the November 2025 changes without a date. BAMF's page still mentions 3 years, so confirm the current rule.

routes.name: Dual citizenship rules
routes.summary: Since 27 June 2024, people naturalized in Germany can generally keep their old citizenship, and Germans can take another without losing German citizenship. Check whether your home country allows it.

other: Your country of origin must also allow multiple citizenship.
German citizenship can be lost only on limited grounds, such as joining a foreign army without permission or fighting for a terrorist group.
Children born in Germany no longer have to choose a citizenship.

sources.label: Federal Foreign Office: law on nationality
BMI: new nationality law takes effect

routes.name: German citizenship by descent
routes.summary: A child born to a German parent is German at birth. If the German parent was born abroad after 31 December 1999 and lives there, the child isn't German automatically unless the birth is registered within 1 year.

other: Child born abroad to a German parent born abroad after 31 Dec 1999: register the birth within one year, or the child would otherwise be stateless.
If only the father is German and paternity must be established, he must acknowledge it before the child turns 23.
Older claims such as Article 116(2) of the Basic Law and section 15 StAG are handled under separate rules, not checked here.

citizenship.note: Generation cut-off applies to parents born abroad after 31 Dec 1999.

sources.label: StAG section 4
Federal Foreign Office: law on nationality

routes.name: German citizenship by birth in Germany
routes.summary: A child born in Germany to foreign parents becomes German if one parent has lived legally in Germany for 5 years and has a permanent residence right. The child keeps the parents' citizenship.

other: At the time of birth, one parent has 5 years of lawful residence and unlimited right of residence.
